title: ADP: Lightweight Decision Broker and Runtime Authorization Filter for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Deliver a lightweight Authorization Decision Broker (ADP) and a paired Runtime Authorization Filter that together provide a single, auditable decision point for API, runtime serving, and Console traffic. The ADP will evaluate RBAC v2 policies (policy language described in the RBAC v2 spec), produce cryptographically-signed decisions for downstream enforcement, emit structured audit events, and expose a small HTTP/gRPC surface for synchronous decisions. The Runtime Authorization Filter integrates into the serving runtime and Console API gateway to enforce decisions with minimal latency, local caching, and graceful fallback to preconfigured policy variants. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, integration tests, and a small canary rollout for internal teams.
acceptance_criteria: ADP runs as a horizontally-scalable service behind existing service mesh and exposes a gRPC and HTTP decision API documented in the design doc
Decision responses include decision_id, allowed:boolean, reasons:list, policy_version, ttl_seconds, and a base64 signature header that receivers can verify
Runtime Authorization Filter enforces decisions and supports a local LRU cache with TTL and negative caching for denied decisions
Audit events emitted for every decision (allow/deny/fallback) to the central audit pipeline in the expected JSON schema (actor, action, resource, policy_id, decision_id, timestamp)
End-to-end latency added by ADP + filter is < 4ms P50 and < 12ms P95 in our staging hardware profile for cached allow decisions
Integration tests that simulate SSO/SAML SCIM-provisioned roles and show policy evaluation results for console, API, and runtime request flows
Feature flags exist to enable/disable ADP enforcement per environment and per customer, with canary rollout plan documented
Security review completed and KMS integration for signing decisions implemented (key rotation documented)
Operational runbook and dashboard with key metrics: decision rate, cache hit ratio, decision latency, signed-verification failures, and audit delivery failures
implementation_notes: Prototype will live in runtime/authorization/decision-broker. Initial implementation uses Envoy ext_authz for Console/API gateway enforcement and a lightweight in-process filter for the serving runtime. We will re-use the policy evaluator library from rbac-v2-eval but add a thin translation layer to canonical ADP inputs. Decisions are signed using KMS-backed keys and verified in the filter. Cache uses an adaptive TTL driven by policy metadata.
work_items: Design ADP public API and signing format (gRPC + HTTP JSON)
Implement ADP service with in-memory policy index and evaluation adapter
Integrate KMS signing and verification in ADP and filter
Add Runtime Authorization Filter to serving runtime with pluggable cache backend
Wire ext_authz for Console/API gateway to the ADP
End-to-end tests including SSO/SAML role mapping scenarios
Dashboard and alerting for decision throughput and audit pipeline health
Canary rollout for internal teams (alpha redwood-internal tenant)
notes: This approach centralizes policy intent while allowing low-latency enforcement via signed decisions and local caches. Trade-offs: central evaluation simplifies policy management and auditability but introduces a new network hop; mitigated via aggressive caching, short-circuit allow paths, and regional ADP replicas. Long-term plan is to evolve ADP into a multi-tenant, rate-limited service with per-customer policy shards.
